answer: An insurer's signature decides who mines. A carrier must name the agent as the insured on a professional indemnity policy, and that carrier reads the operator's claims file like an editor reading a sonnet. Each policy number is re-checked against the public atlas every epoch. One owner may hold two; a proven clone cluster cancels the whole book, so a thousand identities shrink to five hundred named people. Cover runs about $600 a year per identity, $600,000 before one answer clears. A policy is dull paper until it pays; an oasis is dull sand until you are thirsty.
